title: U.S. House · Rhode Island's 2nd District
area: Western and southern Rhode Island, including Warwick, Cranston (part), Newport, West Warwick and South County.

context.text: Incumbent Seth Magaziner (D) advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after Spencer Dickinson did not make the ballot. Victor Mellor (R) won the Republican primary over Stephen Skoly. Armando Anzoli (independent) did not make the ballot. Cook Political Report rates this district D+4.

summary.text: Seth Magaziner is the Democratic incumbent seeking a third term in Rhode Island's 2nd District. A Bristol native, he worked as a teacher and in investment management before serving as Rhode Island's General Treasurer from 2015 to 2023, and he was first elected to the U.S. House in 2022. His official biography describes his work as focused on lowering drug prices, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and abortion rights.

background.text: Born July 22, 1983, in Bristol, Rhode Island, where, according to his official House biography, he grew up.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Brown University (2006) and an MBA from the Yale School of Management (2010).
Taught elementary school in Opelousas, Louisiana, from 2006 to 2008 as a Teach For America member, according to Wikipedia; Ballotpedia lists the employer as the St. Landry Parish School Board.
After business school, worked as a vice president at Trillium Asset Management; earlier, in 2009, he was an associate at the Rhode Island venture capital firm Point Judith Capital.
Won the 2014 Democratic primary for General Treasurer over former treasurer Frank Caprio, then won the general election and served from January 2015 to January 2023, succeeding Gina Raimondo.
His official biography says that as Treasurer he led an initiative to rebuild school buildings across the state and created programs to invest in clean energy projects.

Announced a run for governor in September 2021, withdrew in January 2022 after Rep. James Langevin announced his retirement, and ran for the 2nd District seat instead. He won the September 2022 Democratic primary with 54% of the vote and the November 2022 general election over Republican Allan Fung, 50% to 47%.
Re-elected in 2024 with 58% of the vote over Republican Steve Corvi. Ran unopposed in the September 9, 2026, Democratic primary.
Serves on the House Natural Resources Committee and the Committee on Homeland Security, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Counterterrorism and Intelligence (119th Congress).
According to his official biography, he and his wife Julia have two children. He has served on the boards of Crossroads Rhode Island and, previously, Common Cause Rhode Island.

positions.summary: His official issues page lists support for reinstating the assault weapons ban, universal background checks, safe-storage requirements, limits on high-capacity magazines and silencers, and stronger red flag laws.
positions.quote: Reinstate the ban on assault weapons used in many mass shootings

positions.summary: His official issues page says he is fighting to codify the protections of Roe v. Wade nationally.
His official issues page says he is committed to accelerating the transition to a clean energy future.
positions.quote: committed to accelerating the transition to a clean energy future

positions.summary: Joined Rhode Island health care leaders in calling for extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and restoring Medicaid funding.
Filed an amicus brief at the Supreme Court challenging the President's use of IEEPA to impose sweeping tariffs, saying they raise costs for Rhode Islanders.
positions.quote: Rhode Islanders are being hurt by President Trump’s sweeping tariffs, which are driving up the cost of food, energy, and other everyday essentials,

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Subcommittees on Counterterrorism and Intelligence, and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure) and the House Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Energy and Mineral Resources, and Water, Wildlife and Fisheries).

candidates.name: Victor Mellor

summary.text: Victor (Vic) Mellor is the Republican nominee. A Woonsocket native and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, he worked in the construction business after moving to Florida. He won the September 9, 2026, Republican primary and says he is running on jobs and manufacturing, parental rights, energy costs and healthcare costs.

background.text: Grew up in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, and graduated from Woonsocket High School.

Served in the U.S. Marine Corps as a Sergeant and explosives-detection dog handler stationed in Norfolk, Virginia, including repeated temporary duty with the Presidential Helicopter Squadron (HMX-1) and the Fleet Anti-Terrorism Security Team (FAST), according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

After his military service, built a career in business; Ocean State Media reported that he found success in the construction business after moving to Florida. Ballotpedia lists his career experience as business owner and president.
Is a founding member of the Great American Health Alliance (GAHA), which he says works with medical professionals on strategies to lower the cost of medical care.
Ocean State Media reported, citing a Providence Journal report, that he was present at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. He held a rally in Warwick on March 7, 2026, to promote his campaign.
Won the September 9, 2026, Republican primary with 58.6% of the vote (8,404 votes) over Stephen Skoly.
Reports endorsements from Veterans for America First and the Rhode Island Fraternal Order of Police, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

priorities.text: Building a stronger jobs climate in Rhode Island, including manufacturing and boat-building, to reduce graduate outmigration.
Protecting parental authority over children's physical and mental healthcare decisions.
Lowering healthcare costs, including codifying executive orders on Most Favored Nation drug pricing and hospital billing transparency.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for streamlining years-long permitting processes to speed construction of homes, and says "Build more, regulate less."
positions.quote: Build more, regulate less, own your future.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will work in Congress to block "Red Flag" laws and opposes broad bans, including those targeting so-called "assault weapons."
positions.quote: He will actively work in Congress to block "Red Flag" laws and other measures that violate the fundamental principle of due process by allowing the government to seize property before a person is convicted of a crime.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he supports school choice vouchers and funding for private, charter, or homeschool options.
positions.quote: Vic supports school choice vouchers and funding that give working-class families the power to choose the best private, charter, or homeschool options for their children.

statements.quote: Vic stands for the rule of law, including the immediate removal of criminal illegals. He supports a pathway to permanent residency for law-abiding, tax-paying foreigners.
I also support an energy policy that restores reliable fossil fuel production and use. Renewable sources are intermittent and unreliable.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: Parents should not have to worry about their daughters sharing locker rooms or competing on unfair athletic fields against biological males. Vic will fight to preserve women’s sports and private spaces.
